findings.failure_scenario: crew.py defines `def create_crew() -> Crew:` whose body raises (e.g., an Agent config validation error or a missing env var). Previously the exception propagated to get_crews' per-attribute handler, which printed `Error processing attribute create_crew: <message>`; now the ValueError is caught at line 346 and None is returned, so `crewai reset-memories` reports only 'No crew found.' and the user gets no indication of the real error that broke their crew.
findings.summary: get_crew_instance's blanket `except Exception: return None` silently swallows exceptions raised by a user's crew factory function, deleting the error report the old code printed.

findings.failure_scenario: A project containing a local module that shadows an installed dependency (e.g., a `crewai/` or `tomli.py` directory at the project root or under src/) — after get_crews runs, every later import in the CLI process (crew.py exec, tool extraction, memory reset) resolves to the user's copy. In the crewai-checkout dev case, `import crewai` inside the exec'd module resolves to checkout `src/crewai`, a different class object than the running CLI's Crew, so `isinstance(module_attr, Crew)` fails and the CLI reports 'No valid Crew instance found' for a valid project.
findings.summary: get_crews permanently inserts the cwd and cwd/src at the front of sys.path with no cleanup, so project files can hijack imports for the rest of the CLI process.

findings.failure_scenario: Project with `crew.py` (crew A) and `marketing/crew.py` (crew B): the old code collected crews from every crew.py under '.', but the new `if crew_instances: break` stops at the first productive file, so `crewai reset-memories --all` resets only crew A's memories and silently leaves crew B's stale memories in place.
findings.summary: Breaking out of the walk after the first crew.py file that yields a crew silently drops crews defined in other crew.py files, a regression from the previous whole-tree aggregation.

findings.failure_scenario: In test_get_crews_ignores_template_directories the fixture's crew.py files raise at import (Crew(agents=[], tasks=[]) is invalid), so the walk reaches src/templates/crew.py; since 'cli/templates' is not a substring of root 'src/templates', that file IS processed and the mocked fetch_crews returns a crew for its dunder attributes — the crews 'found' come from the template file itself. The assertion only passes because the detector checks module_attr.__file__, which none of the comment-only module's attributes have; the test would still pass even though template files are loaded.
findings.summary: The template-exclusion check `"cli/templates" not in root` does not exclude the `src/templates` layout its own new test uses, and test_get_crews_ignores_template_directories passes vacuously, so the claimed ignore-templates behavior is unverified.

findings.failure_scenario: Running the CLI from the crewai source checkout on Windows: os.walk yields roots like `src\crewai\cli\templates`, which do not contain the substring 'cli/templates', so the template crew.py (whose `{{crew_name}}` class name is a SyntaxError) is executed as if it were the user's crew, producing 'Error executing module: invalid syntax' noise and a misleading 'No valid Crew instance found' instead of a clean skip.
findings.summary: The hardcoded forward slash in `"cli/templates" not in root` never matches on Windows, where os.walk yields backslash-separated roots, so the template exclusion silently does nothing there.

findings.failure_scenario: User's crew.py raises `NameError: name 'x' is not defined` on line 42 of a helper module; the CLI now prints only 'Error executing module: name x is not defined' with no traceback, where the old code printed the full traceback identifying the failing file and line — materially harder for CLI users to debug their own crew.py.
findings.summary: The rewrite of the module-execution error handler dropped the `traceback.format_exc()` output the old code printed, so users lose file/line context when their crew.py fails to import.

findings.failure_scenario: In test_get_crews_finds_valid_crews, exec of the fixture's root and src crew.py both fail with PydanticCustomError('missing_keys'); the only crews returned come from the mocked fetch_crews applied to dunder attributes of the comment-only src/templates/crew.py — the test asserts len(crews) > 0 without any valid crew module ever loading, so a regression that broke loading real Crew instances would go undetected.
findings.summary: The fixture's `direct_crew = Crew(agents=[], tasks=[])` violates crewai's own check_config validation ('Either agents and tasks need to be set or config'), so every fixture crew.py raises at import and get_crews' success path is never actually exercised by the new tests.

findings.failure_scenario: Project with no root crew.py and a src/crew.py that does module-level work (API call, print, resource init) but yields no Crew instance: the file is exec'd once as './src/crew.py' during the '.' walk and again as 'src/crew.py' during the second search path, doubling side effects and import cost before the 'No valid Crew instance found' exit.
findings.summary: The `src` search path is redundant with the '.' walk (os.walk('.') already descends into src), so when no crew is found the same src modules are imported and executed a second time, running their module-level side effects twice.
